description: Cross-modulator: two signals combined by one of nine algorithms, from crossfading and wavefolding through ring modulation and bit crushing to a twenty-band vocoder

params.text: Sweeps continuously through the nine algorithms marked around it, and in the vocoder sets the release time of its envelope followers
Sets how strongly the cross-modulation products are produced, and in the vocoder shifts the formants taken from the modulator
Switches the internal oscillator on and steps through its waveforms; with it off, the carrier input is used instead
Sets the gain of the carrier input, or the frequency of the internal oscillator over five octaves when that is running
Sets the gain of the modulator input, and gains above unity overdrive it

inputs.text: Adds to the carrier gain, 5V for full; with the internal oscillator running it sets that oscillator's pitch at one volt per octave
Adds to the modulator gain, 5V for full
Sweeps the algorithm, 5V covering the whole range, added to the ALGORITHM knob
Adds to the TIMBRE knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
The carrier audio; with the internal oscillator running, this signal phase-modulates it instead

outputs.text: The two signals combined by the chosen algorithm
The sum of the carrier and modulator after their gain stages, or the bare internal oscillator when that is running

notes: with the internal oscillator switched off, nothing comes out until audio is patched into both the carrier and the modulator inputs.
pressing the oscillator button puts the internal oscillator in place of the carrier input.
this module has no right-click menu of its own; the algorithm and the internal oscillator are set on the panel.
the module is monophonic: on a polyphonic cable only the first channel is processed.
